subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why must a transformer use an alternating current in the primary coil?
options: To keep the iron core cool
To create a continuously changing magnetic field that induces a p.d. in the secondary
questions.explain: A transformer works only with a changing magnetic field. Alternating current produces a continually changing field in the iron core, which induces an alternating p.d. in the secondary coil. A steady dc would give no induced p.d. after switch-on.

questions.q: What is the shape of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire?
options: A field like a bar magnet
questions.explain: A current in a straight wire produces a magnetic field of concentric circles around the wire. The field is stronger nearer the wire and with a larger current.

questions.q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, what does the THUMB represent?
questions.explain: Fleming's left-hand rule: First finger = Field, seCond finger = Current, thuMb = Motion (force). It gives the direction of the force on the conductor.

questions.q: As light intensity falling on a light-dependent resistor (LDR) increases, its resistance:
questions.explain: An LDR's resistance decreases as light intensity increases (high resistance in the dark, low resistance in bright light). This is used in light-sensing circuits.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
questions.explain: Current is an SI base quantity and its base unit is the ampere (A). The coulomb (charge), volt (p.d.) and ohm (resistance) are derived units.

questions.q: Which statement about direct current (dc) and alternating current (ac) is correct?
options: ac constantly reverses direction; dc is one direction
Both flow in one direction only
dc constantly reverses direction; ac is one direction
questions.explain: Alternating current (ac) constantly changes direction, while direct current (dc), such as from a cell or battery, flows in one direction only.

questions.q: What did the alpha particle scattering experiment lead Rutherford to conclude?
options: Atoms are a ball of positive charge with electrons embedded in it
Mass and positive charge are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus
Electrons orbit at fixed distances in shells
questions.explain: Most alpha particles passed straight through but a few were deflected back, showing the atom is mostly empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus — replacing the plum pudding model.

questions.q: Which component is represented by a circle with a cross inside it?
questions.explain: A filament lamp is shown as a circle with a cross inside. A diode is a triangle pointing to a line, and a fuse is a rectangle with a line through it.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-contact force?
questions.explain: A non-contact force acts without objects touching. Gravitational force acts at a distance; friction, air resistance and tension all require contact.

questions.q: In a parallel circuit with two branches connected across a battery, the potential difference across each branch is:
options: Larger across the branch with more resistance only
questions.explain: In parallel, each branch is connected directly across the supply, so the potential difference across each branch is the same. The current divides between the branches.

questions.q: Which action will induce a potential difference in a coil of wire? (generator effect)
options: Holding a stationary magnet inside the coil
Leaving the coil in a steady magnetic field
Placing the coil far from any magnet
Moving a magnet into or out of the coil
questions.explain: A potential difference is induced only when there is a change in the magnetic field through the coil, e.g. moving a magnet in or out. A stationary magnet causes no induced p.d.

questions.q: What is the best tool for plotting the shape and direction of a magnetic field around a bar magnet?
questions.explain: A plotting compass needle aligns with the field at each point, letting you trace the field lines and their direction. Iron filings show the shape but not the direction.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a thermistor as its temperature rises?
questions.explain: For a typical (NTC) thermistor, resistance decreases as temperature increases. This is used in temperature-sensing circuits such as thermostats.

questions.q: Two identical resistors are connected in parallel. How does the total resistance compare with that of a single resistor?
questions.explain: Adding resistors in parallel provides more paths for charge to flow, so the total resistance is less than the smallest individual resistor (for two equal resistors, it is half).

questions.q: Which device uses a split-ring commutator to produce direct current as a coil rotates?
questions.explain: A dc dynamo (generator) uses a split-ring commutator, which swaps the coil's connections every half turn so the output current always flows the same way — direct current. An alternator uses slip rings and gives ac.

questions.q: What does the I-V characteristic of a diode show?
options: Current flows equally in both directions
Current flows freely in one direction only
questions.explain: A diode has very high resistance in the reverse direction, so it only allows appreciable current to flow in one (forward) direction.

questions.q: How can you reverse the direction of the force on a wire in an electric motor?
options: It is impossible to reverse the force
Only by switching off the current
By reversing either the current OR the magnetic field direction
questions.explain: Reversing the current direction or the magnetic field direction reverses the force. (Reversing both at once returns the force to its original direction.)

questions.q: The motor effect produces the LARGEST force on a current-carrying wire when the wire is...
questions.explain: The force is greatest when the wire is perpendicular (90°) to the field. When the wire is parallel to the field, the force is zero.

questions.q: Light reflecting evenly off a smooth mirror to form a clear image is an example of:
questions.explain: A smooth surface like a mirror reflects parallel rays in a single direction, giving specular (regular) reflection and a clear image. A rough surface scatters light (diffuse reflection).

questions.q: What happens to the induced potential difference if the direction in which a magnet moves through a coil is reversed?
questions.explain: Reversing the motion (or the magnet's poles) reverses the direction of the induced p.d. This is why a coil rotating in a field produces alternating current.

questions.q: How can you increase the size of the induced potential difference from a generator?
options: Use fewer turns on the coil
Move the magnet faster, use more turns, or use a stronger magnet
Move the magnet or coil more slowly
questions.explain: A larger induced p.d. results from a faster rate of change of the field, more turns on the coil, or a stronger magnet — all increase how quickly field lines are cut.

questions.q: An atom is electrically neutral. This is because it has an equal number of...
options: neutrons and protons in the nucleus only
questions.explain: Atoms are neutral because they contain equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons, so the charges cancel.
